heroData.title: Hire in Netherlands (Payrolling)
heroData.subtitle: WAADI & Inlenerbeloning
heroData.description: Strict equal pay laws (Inlenerbeloning) mean EOR staff must match internal salary/benefits. EOR provider takes on legal employer risk.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting of an employment contract that complies with the Dutch Civil Code and any applicable Collective Labor Agreement (CAO). Contracts can be fixed-term or indefinite.

steps.title: Identity & Right to Work
steps.description: Verification of a valid passport (not ID card for non-EU) and BSN (Burgerservicenummer). For non-EU, verification of the 'Kennismigrant' or work permit status.

steps.title: 30% Ruling Assessment
steps.description: Evaluating if the employee meets the salary and distance criteria (resided >150km from Dutch border for 16/24 months) for the 30% tax-free allowance.

steps.title: Inlenerbeloning Comparison
steps.description: Matching the employee's salary and benefits to the client's internal wage scale to ensure compliance with equal pay regulations for agency workers.

steps.title: Insurance & Pension Setup
steps.description: Enrollment in mandatory social security and the specific industry pension fund (StiPP or a sector-specific fund like ABP/PFZW).

items.title: WAADI Registration
items.text: All companies providing personnel in the Netherlands must be registered with the KvK with a 'WAADI' note. Failing to do so results in heavy fines for both provider and client.

items.title: Chain Rule (Ketenregeling)
items.text: A maximum of 3 temporary contracts can be offered within a 3-year period. The 4th contract or a contract exceeding 3 years automatically becomes permanent.

items.title: Transition Payment
items.text: Since 2020, employees are entitled to a transition payment (severance) from day one of employment, even if the contract is not renewed by the employer.

items.title: Sick Leave Liability
items.text: The legal employer (EOR) is responsible for 104 weeks of sick pay at 70-100% of the salary. Clients must ensure their EOR has robust 'Arbodienst' coverage.

faqs.question: Can I use EOR for contractors?
faqs.answer: No, EOR is for employment. For contractors, you should use 'Compliance' or 'Agent' services to manage the 'Wet DBA' risks of false self-employment.

faqs.question: Does the 30% ruling apply through an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the EOR is a registered withholding agent and the employee meets the specific criteria (salary threshold, migration distance, expertise).

faqs.question: What is the notice period for Dutch EOR?
faqs.answer: Statutory notice is usually 1 month for the employee. For the employer, it increases with tenure (1 to 4 months), but CAOs may specify different terms.

items.title: Direct Communication
items.text: Dutch culture is famously direct. Feedback is often given bluntly without the US-style 'praise sandwich'. This is seen as efficient, not rude, and is expected across all levels of the organization.

items.title: Poldermodel
items.text: A culture of consensus. Decisions are often discussed extensively with all stakeholders, including works councils (Ondernemingsraad). It may slow down initial decisions but ensures smooth implementation.

items.title: Work-Life Balance
items.text: Part-time work is extremely common, especially among parents. The 4-day (32 hour) or even 3-day work week is highly standardized and protected by law. Meetings are rarely scheduled after 5 PM.

items.title: Meeting Culture
items.text: Meetings start exactly on time. Being one minute late without notice is considered disrespectful. Agendas are strictly followed.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Flat organizational structures are the norm. Employees at all levels are encouraged to speak up and challenge senior management if they believe there is a better way.

steps.title: Data Collection & Validation
steps.description: Gathering all monthly mutations including overtime hours, sickness reports, and bonus payments. All data must be validated against the employment contract and any applicable CAO (Collective Labor Agreement) rules.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Detailed calculation involving the Zvw (Employer and Employee Health Insurance Act), WW (Unemployment insurance), WIA (Disability insurance), and the complex progressive income tax rates. Deductions for pensions and company cars (Bijtelling) are also applied at this stage.

steps.title: Loonaangifte Submission
steps.description: The 'Loonaangifte' is an XML-based electronic submission containing detailed per-employee data sent to the Belastingdienst. This must be done within 30 days after the end of the payroll month.

steps.title: Payment & SEPA Execution
steps.description: Generating SEPA payment files for net salary transfers. Payments are usually scheduled for the 24th or 25th of the month. Concurrently, the wage tax payment is scheduled for the tax authorities.

steps.title: Annual Year-End Reporting
steps.description: Consolidating all monthly data into the annual 'Jaaropgave' (Annual Statement) for employees, which they use for their personal income tax returns.

items.title: 8% Holiday Allowance
items.text: Mandatory 'Vakantiegeld' (Holiday Pay) is 8% of the total gross wage, usually paid as a lump sum in May or June.

items.title: 30% Ruling Decapping
items.text: Be aware of the 'Balkenende norm' (WNT) capping of the 30% ruling for salaries over €233,000 (2024 value) and the gradual reduction from 30% to 10% over 5 years.

items.title: Work-Related Costs Scheme (WKR)
items.text: Employers can provide tax-free benefits up to a certain 'free space' (vrije ruimte). Exceeding this triggers an 80% final levy for the employer.

items.title: Travel Allowance
items.text: Tax-free reimbursement for commuting up to €0.23 per kilometer for 2025. Alternatively, public transport cards (NS Business Card) are common.

items.title: Commuting via Bicycle
items.text: Deeply cultural. Many employers offer a 'Bicycle Plan' or the 'Fietsplan' where employees buy a bike from gross salary.

items.title: Home Office Allowance
items.text: A tax-free allowance of €2.35 per day (2025 rate) is allowed for employees working from home.

items.title: Social Security Caps 2025
items.text: The maximum premium wages for employees is capped. For 2025, the cap is approximately €71,628 (subject to final year-end adjustments).

items.title: Holiday Pay (Vakantiegeld)
items.text: Mandatory 8% holiday allowance, usually paid out in May. The gross salary mentioned in contracts must explicitly state if it includes or excludes this amount.

items.title: Sector-Specific Social Security
items.text: The 'Whk' (Werkhervattingskas) rate varies by sector and company size. High-risk sectors pay more.

items.title: Pension Franchise
items.text: Pension isn't calculated on the whole salary. A 'franchise' (threshold of ~€17k) is subtracted first.

items.title: Minimum Wage 2025
items.text: Minimum wage is determined per hour. For 2025, it is €13.68 (estimated) per hour for 21+ years old.

steps.title: Determine Gross Base
steps.description: Starting with the agreed monthly salary excluding holiday pay.

steps.title: Add Mandatory Loaders
steps.description: Adding 8.33% for vacation days and 8% for holiday allowance.

steps.title: Apply 30% Ruling
steps.description: If applicable, move 30% of the taxable amount to the tax-free column.

faqs.question: What is the net take-home on €50,000?
faqs.answer: Assuming standard tax credits and no 30% ruling, the net is approximately €3,250 per month (including holiday pay reservation).

faqs.question: Does the calculator include Zvw?
faqs.answer: Yes, our simulation includes both the employer-paid Zvw (6.10%) and the employee contribution.

faqs.question: What about commute tax?
faqs.answer: Travel allowances are typically calculated separately as they are tax-free and based on actual distance.

items.title: Bijtelling 2025
items.text: Addition to taxable income for the private use of a company car. For 2025, the standard rate is 22% of the Dutch list price (incl. VAT and BPM). Electric vehicles (EVs) may have a lower capped rate of 17% for the first €30,000.

items.title: WKR (Work-Related Expenses Scheme)
items.text: Allows employers to provide tax-free benefits (e.g., gym memberships, bicycles) up to a certain 'free space' percentage of the total wage bill. In 2025, the free space for the first €400,000 of the wage bill is likely around 1.92%.

items.title: Salary Thresholds
items.text: High salary thresholds apply for highly skilled migrants. In 2025, the threshold for those over 30 is ~€5,350 per month, and for those under 30, it is ~€3,925 (excluding holiday pay).

items.title: 30% Ruling Cap
items.text: From 2024 onwards, the 30% ruling is capped at the 'Balkenende norm' (€233,000 in 2024/2025). Income above this level is fully taxable.

steps.title: Wage Tax Number
steps.description: Applying for a 'Loonheffingennummer' from the Belastingdienst before the first payday.

steps.title: ID Verification
steps.description: Strict requirement to verify and archive a physical copy of the employee's ID (passport/ID card, not driver's license).

steps.title: Pension Registration
steps.description: Reporting new hires to the industry-wide pension fund (Stichting Pensioenfonds) if applicable to your sector.

heroData.title: Setup a Dutch BV
heroData.subtitle: Besloten Vennootschap
heroData.description: The BV is the standard limited liability company. No minimum capital requirement (symbolic €0.01).

steps.title: KYC & Structure Confirmation
steps.description: Providing identification for all UBOs (Ultimate Beneficial Owners) and directors to the Notary. Definition of the share capital (e.g., €100 split into 100 shares).

steps.title: Deed of Incorporation
steps.description: The Civil Law Notary prepares the 'Statuten'. Signing can be done via Power of Attorney (POA) for foreign founders.

steps.title: KvK Registration
steps.description: The Notary registers the new entity with the Kamer van Koophandel. A KvK number is issued immediately upon processing.

steps.title: UBO Register Filing
steps.description: Mandatory registration of individuals holding >25% interest or significant control. Failure to file prevents bank account opening.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: Auto-registration with the Belastingdienst for Corporate Tax (VPB) and VAT (BTW). VAT numbers take 2-4 weeks to arrive.

items.title: BV vs Branch
items.text: A BV is a separate legal person, shielding the parent. A Branch (Filiaal) is part of the parent company, with shared liability but simpler annual filing.

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: While there is no legal requirement for a Dutch resident director, most banks will reject applications without at least one local representative or local substance.

items.title: Flex-BV
items.text: Since 2012, BV laws are extremely flexible. You can issue shares with and without voting rights or profit rights.

faqs.question: Can a foreign company be the sole shareholder?
faqs.answer: Yes, a foreign legal entity (HoldCo) can own 100% of the Dutch BV. You will need to provide notarized/apostilled corporate documents of the parent.

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: This is the longest part! Standard banks (ING, ABN Amro, Rabobank) take 2-3 months. FinTechs (Bunq, Revolut) take 1-2 weeks.

faqs.question: Do I need to visit the Netherlands to incorporate?
faqs.answer: No. Everything including Notary signing can be done remotely via legalized Power of Attorney (civil law countries) or Apostille.

items.title: Real Office Requirement
items.text: For tax substance, the company should ideally have its own dedicated office space rather than just a registered address at a trust office.

items.title: eHerkenning Level
items.text: Most tax filings require eHerkenning Level 3 (EH3). Applying for this requires a valid KvK registration and a physical appointment for the legal representative.

heroData.title: Recruitment (Werving & Selectie)
heroData.subtitle: Highly Skilled Migrants
heroData.description: Tech market is tight. Agencies help source local Dutch talent or relocate Knowledge Migrants (Kennismigrant).

steps.title: Profile Sourcing
steps.description: Defining the role according to Dutch market standards. Sourcing via LinkedIn, local job boards (Indeed.nl), and specialized niche networks.

steps.title: Screening & Cultural Fit
steps.description: Two-stage interview process focusing on technical skills and direct Dutch communication style fit. Verify salary expectations against benchmark.

steps.title: Sponsorship Check
steps.description: Determining if the candidate requires a Highly Skilled Migrant visa (IND sponsorship) and if the employer/EOR has the status.

steps.title: Offer & Contract
steps.description: Issuing the offer letter. Unlike the US, a signed employment contract is the primary legal document in the NL.

items.title: Shortage Occupations
items.text: Software development, renewable energy engineering, and healthcare are 'Kansrijke Beroepen' with extreme shortages.

items.title: Highly Skilled Migrant Thresholds 2025
items.text: Minimum gross salary for KM visa: €5,331 (over 30), €3,909 (under 30), and €2,801 (recent NL grads).

items.title: Non-Compete Restrictions
items.text: New legislation aims to restrict non-competes. They are generally only valid in permanent contracts with specific geographic and duration limits.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period employees give?
faqs.answer: The statutory notice period is 1 month, starting from the end of the calendar month. Highly senior roles often have 2-3 months negotiated.

faqs.question: Can I hire a candidate without a local entity?
faqs.answer: Only if you use an EOR partner that is a 'Recognized Sponsor' with the IND (Immigration and Naturalization Service).

faqs.question: Is English enough for the Dutch market?
faqs.answer: In Amsterdam/Tech/Finance, yes. In Sales/Operations or outside Randstad, Dutch is often mandatory for relationship building.

items.title: IND Recognised Sponsor
items.text: To hire highly skilled migrants from outside the EU, the employer must be a 'Recognised Sponsor' with the IND. This requires an application and a one-time fee.

items.title: 2025 Salary Thresholds
items.text: Minimum gross monthly salary for migrants >30 years is €5,410 (excluding holiday allowance). For <30 years, it is €3,969. These are indexed annually.

heroData.title: HR Systems
heroData.subtitle: Leave & Sickness
heroData.description: Systems must track 'Wet verbetering poortwachter' steps for sick employees strictly.

items.title: Nmbrs & AFAS
items.text: Dominant local players. AFAS is ERP-heavy; Nmbrs is popular for its HR-Payroll workflow integration.

items.title: Poortwachter Compliance
items.text: HRIS must trigger alerts at week 6, week 8, week 42, and week 88 of sick leave to avoid UWV wage sanctions (up to 1 year extra pay).

items.title: GDPR Compliance (AVG)
items.text: The Dutch DPA (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) is very strict. Data residency and strict access controls for 'special categories' are required.

steps.title: Requirement Mapping
steps.description: Auditing existing spreadsheets/systems. Defining leave policies (Statutory 20 days vs CAO-extra days).

steps.title: Payroll Integration
steps.description: Setting up the API link between HRIS and the Payroll engine (e.g., Personio to Nmbrs) for automated mutations.

steps.title: Self-Service Rollout
steps.description: Granting employee access for leave requests, expense claims, and digital signature of addendums.

steps.title: Reporting Setup
steps.description: Configuring 'Verzuim' (Absenteeism) reports and FTE breakdowns for KvK/Annual filing requirements.

faqs.question: Does HRIS handle the 30% ruling?
faqs.answer: Most local Dutch HRIS tools (Nmbrs, AFAS) have a specific toggle to apply the 30% ruling automatically to the gross-to-net calculation.

faqs.question: Can I use US-based HRIS like Rippling?
faqs.answer: Yes, but ensure it has a Dutch localized payroll connector or exports a format compatible with Dutch payroll providers (Loonaangifte).

faqs.question: Is digital signing legal for contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Qualified Electronic Signatures' (QES) are fully valid under eIDAS and Dutch law for employment contracts.

items.title: Identity Verification
items.text: Employers are legally required to keep a copy of the front and back of a valid ID (passport or ID card). A driver's license is not sufficient for right-to-work checks.

items.title: Exit Interviews
items.text: While not legally required, exit interviews are highly recommended to prevent potential dismissal disputes and gather feedback on company culture.

heroData.title: Bookkeeping (Administratie)
heroData.subtitle: VAT & Annual Accounts
heroData.description: Quarterly VAT (BTW) filings and Annual Accounts (Jaarrekening) deposited at KvK.

steps.title: Quarterly VAT (BTW)
steps.description: Filing of value-added tax returns. Due by the 30th of the month following the quarter end (April, July, October, January).

steps.title: Annual Accounts Preparation
steps.description: Preparing the Balance Sheet and P&L according to Dutch GAAP. Usually finalized within 5 months of year-end.

steps.title: Corporation Tax (VPB)
steps.description: Filing the annual CIT returns. Provisional assessments are often paid throughout the year based on estimates.

steps.title: KvK Publication
steps.description: Depositing an abridged version of the balance sheet at the Chamber of Commerce. Public access is mandatory for all BV entities.

items.title: Audit Thresholds
items.text: Mandatory audit only if 2 of 3 met: Assets >€7.5M, Revenue >€15M, Employees >50. Most SMEs are exempt.

items.title: Dutch GAAP vs IFRS
items.text: NL GAAP is closer to IFRS but allows historical cost accounting for buildings. SMEs prefer NL GAAP for its simplicity.

items.title: Reverse Charge VAT
items.text: Foreign providers often use the reverse charge mechanism. Incorrect handling leads to VAT liabilities even if it should have been 0%. Verification of VIES status is required.

items.title: UBL E-Invoicing
items.text: Standard format for Dutch e-invoices is UBL 2.1. Most local software (Exact, Twinfield) generates this automatically.

faqs.question: Do I need a local accountant?
faqs.answer: Technically no, but for filing with the Tax Office and KvK, specific local software and electronic signatures (eHerkenning) are required, which local firms manage.

faqs.question: What is eHerkenning?
faqs.answer: It's the mandatory digital ID for businesses in the NL to communicate with government portals. It usually takes 2 weeks to apply for.

faqs.question: Can I use Xero or QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they need to be bridged to Dutch VAT filing tools or Exact Online/Twinfield to be fully compliant with local reporting schemas.

items.title: Peppol Network
items.text: B2G (Business to Government) e-invoicing is mandatory in the Netherlands via the Peppol network. B2B is not yet mandatory but highly encouraged.

items.title: Storage requirements
items.text: Business records and invoices must be kept for 7 years. For real estate records, the period is 10 years.

steps.title: Problem Analysis (Week 6)
steps.description: Occupational Physician (Arbo) evaluates the employee's ability to return to work.

steps.title: Plan of Action (Week 8)
steps.description: Employer and employee agree on reintegration steps (adjusting hours, different tasks).

steps.title: First Year Review (Week 52)
steps.description: Evaluating 'First Track' (return to current employer) vs 'Second Track' (finding a new employer).

steps.title: WIA Application (Week 93)
steps.description: Employee applies for disability benefits; UWV audits if employer did enough. Failure results in 1-year wage penalty.

items.title: Preventative Review
items.text: Unilateral dismissal is rare. Most terminations happen via a 'Vaststellingsovereenkomst' (Settlement Agreement) with at least 1 month notice + transition pay.

items.title: UWV Ground
items.text: Dismissal for economic reasons or long-term disability (2 years+) goes through the UWV. Performance issues go through the District Court.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Max 1 month for contracts <2 years. Max 2 months for indefinite contracts. No probation allowed for contracts <6 months.

faqs.question: Can I fire an employee for poor performance immediately?
faqs.answer: No. You must build a 'dossier' showing feedback, improvement plans, and training over a reasonable period (typically 3-6 months).

faqs.question: What is the 'Wet DBA'?
faqs.answer: It regulates the relationship between clients and freelancers (ZZP). Since 2025, enforcement against false self-employment has become very strict.

faqs.question: Are verbal contracts valid?
faqs.answer: Technically yes, but virtually impossible to prove. Written contracts are required for specific clauses like non-competes or probation.

items.title: Sick Leave Privacy
items.text: Employers may NOT ask for the diagnosis of a sick employee. Only the Occupational Physician (Arbo) can discuss medical details.

items.title: Data Processing Register
items.text: Companies must maintain a register of all processing activities involving employee personal data, including third-party payroll providers.

items.title: Works Council Rights
items.text: The Works Council has a 'Right of Consent' (instemmingsrecht) on any new system that monitors employee performance or attendance.

items.title: WBSO R&D Credit
items.text: Reduction in wage tax for employees doing R&D. Can cover up to 40% of salary costs for startups.

items.title: Participation Exemption
items.text: Dividends and capital gains from subsidiaries (5%+) are 100% tax-exempt in the Netherlands. Key for holding companies.

items.title: Dividend Retraction
items.text: Standard Dividend Withholding Tax is 15%, but is often reduced to 0% under treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.

items.title: Fiscal Unity
items.text: Group companies can be treated as a single taxpayer, allowing for loss-offsetting between profitable and non-profitable entities.

steps.title: VAT Eligibility Check
steps.description: Confirming if your service is subject to 21% (Standard), 9% (Books/Food), or 0% / Exempted (Finance/Medical).

steps.title: Tax Identification Request
steps.description: Applying for the BTW-ID (for invoicing) and the BTW-nummer (for communication with authorities).

steps.title: ICP Filing
steps.description: Extra filing for supplies to other EU countries (Intra-Community Transactions) to track VAT-free cross-border sales.

faqs.question: What is the small business scheme (KOR)?
faqs.answer: If your turnover is <€20,000/year, you can be exempt from VAT obligations, but you cannot reclaim input VAT either.

faqs.question: How long can losses be carried forward?
faqs.answer: Since 2022, losses can be carried forward indefinitely, but the offset is capped at 50% of profit exceeding €1M.

faqs.question: What is the 30% ruling cost to the employer?
faqs.answer: The ruling is tax-neutral for the employer, but reduces the gross salary basis for employer social security contributions.

items.title: Standard Year
items.text: The fiscal year usually matches the calendar year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). Deviating fiscal years are allowed but require Notarial deed specification.

items.title: Loss Carry Back
items.text: Losses can be carried back for 1 year, providing a direct refund of taxes paid in the previous profitable year. Highly effective for cash-flow management during downturns.

items.title: Interest Limitation
items.text: Net interest expenses are deductible up to the higher of 20% of EBITDA or €1 million (Earnings Stripping Rule).

heroData.title: Dutch Law
heroData.subtitle: Contract Law
heroData.description: Civil code based. Contracts are generally binding and interpreted by 'reasonableness and fairness'.

items.title: Reasonableness & Fairness
items.text: The principle of 'Redelijkheid en Billijkheid' allows courts to set aside contractual terms if they are considered unacceptable in given circumstances.

items.title: Transfer of Undertaking (overgang van onderneming)
items.text: In asset deals, employees automatically transfer to the buyer with all existing rights and obligations. You cannot cherry-pick employees.

items.title: Share Deal vs Asset Deal
items.text: Share deals are more common for larger entities (liability stays in BV). Asset deals allow the buyer to leave behind specific liabilities.

steps.title: Letter of Intent (LOI)
steps.description: Defining deal structure, price mechanism (locked box vs completion accounts), and exclusivity period.

steps.title: Due Diligence
steps.description: Financial, Legal, and Fiscal audit. In NL, 'Vendor Due Diligence' is common to speed up the process.

steps.title: Works Council Consultation
steps.description: Mandatory 'Adviesaanvraag' (advice request) if the company has a works council. The deal cannot close until advice is rendered.

steps.title: Signing & Closing
steps.description: Signing the Share Purchase Agreement (SPA). Closing involves Notarial transfer for BVs.

faqs.question: What is the 4% Real Estate Transfer Tax on shares?
faqs.answer: Since 2025, share deals in real-estate-heavy companies (where RE >50% of value) trigger a 4% RETT to prevent tax avoidance.

faqs.question: Are choice-of-law clauses (e.g. English Law) allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for Dutch employment matters or Dutch real estate, specific mandatory local laws will always prevail.

faqs.question: Is arbitration common?
faqs.answer: Yes, via the NAI (Netherlands Arbitration Institute) or specialized courts like the NCC (Netherlands Commercial Court) which allows proceedings in English.

items.title: Harmonization of Benefits
items.text: Harmonizing employment terms after an acquisition is complex due to the 'No Disadvantage' principle in Dutch labor law. Any decrease in secondary benefits must often be compensated.

items.title: Works Council Role
items.text: The Works Council must be consulted on any significant organizational changes post-merger, including changes in management or reporting structures. This consultation must be timely to be meaningful.

items.title: Cultural Integration
items.text: Merging a Dutch company with a foreign parent often requires a focused effort on integrating different management styles, specifically moving from top-down to consensus-based.

items.title: Redundancy Rules
items.text: If the merger leads to redundancies, the 'Last-In-First-Out' (Afspiegelingsbeginsel) principle must be strictly applied within interchangeable categories of roles.

heroData.title: Tech Hub
heroData.subtitle: Amsterdam/Eindhoven
heroData.description: Eindhoven (Brainport) is a major hardware/tech hub. Amsterdam is key for SaaS/Fintech.

items.title: Connectivity Peak
items.text: AMS-IX is the world's leading Internet Exchange. The NL has the highest broadband penetration in Europe.

items.title: Eindhoven Brainport
items.text: World-leading for DeepTech/Hardware. ASML and Philips ecosystems drive massive demand for embedded software engineers.

items.title: AI Act Readiness
items.text: The Dutch supervisor (AP) is proactive on AI. Ensure ML models comply with biased data restrictions under new EU guidelines.

steps.title: Localization Review
steps.description: Ensuring UI supports Dutch language and local formatting (date/currency) if targeting SMEs.

steps.title: Integration with Identity
steps.description: Integrating with DigiD (Citizen ID) or eHerkenning (Business ID) for government-facing SasS.

steps.title: GDPR Audit
steps.description: Implementing 'Processing Agreements' and ensuring high-availability within EU-based data centers (often Eemshaven or Amsterdam).

faqs.question: What are the top Fintech hubs?
faqs.answer: Amsterdam is home to Adyen, Mollie, and Bunq. The city has a strong talent pool specifically for payment infrastructure.

faqs.question: Is the startup visa available?
faqs.answer: Yes, for innovative software founders with a facilitator and enough capital to live on for the first year.

faqs.question: Can I use contractor devs?
faqs.answer: Yes, but due to 'Wet DBA', avoid long-term (>1 year) exclusive relationships that look like employment without benefits.

items.title: NLNOG (NL Network Operators Group)
items.text: The Netherlands has one of the most robust network operator communities in the world, ensuring high availability and low latency.

items.title: BSI / ISO Certification
items.text: Dutch B2B clients heavily favor service providers with ISO 27001 or NEN 7510 (specifically for healthcare data) certifications.

items.title: Data Retention Laws
items.text: Be aware of local Dutch implementation of EU data retention directives, especially if providing communication services.

heroData.title: Digital Growth
heroData.subtitle: English Proficiency
heroData.description: Dutch market accepts English marketing well, but localization builds trust significantly. The Dutch consumer is pragmatic and values transparency above all.

items.title: Directness in Copy
items.text: The Dutch value clarity and pragmatism over hyperbole. Avoid 'World's Number One' unless you can prove it with independent data.

items.title: B2B LinkedIn Culture
items.text: Very high penetration. Personal social selling by founders is more effective in NL than corporate ads. Content should be informative, not salesy.

items.title: Influencer Transparency
items.text: Stricter guidelines (CvdM) require clear labeling of 'Paid Partnership' even for gifted items for micro-influencers.

steps.title: Market Benchmarking
steps.description: Analyzing CPC for Dutch keywords. Keywords in Dutch are often 30-50% cheaper but have lower volume.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Setup
steps.description: Implementing Dutch-language landing pages and localized payment proof (iDEAL logos).

steps.title: Testing & Iteration
steps.description: Running A/B tests between informal 'je/jij' and formal 'u' addressing.

faqs.question: Why is iDEAL important?
faqs.answer: Over 70% of Dutch online transactions happen via iDEAL. Without the logo, trust drops significantly. It is the gold standard for Dutch consumer confidence.

faqs.question: Best city for agencies?
faqs.answer: Amsterdam is the creative capital, with many global agencies headquartered there. Rotterdam is emerging for specialized industrial and logistics marketing.

faqs.question: What is the typical lead time for a campaign?
faqs.answer: Standard digital campaigns can be launched in 2-4 weeks, while full brand localization usually requires 8-12 weeks.

faqs.question: Do I need a local VAT number for advertising?
faqs.answer: If you are a non-EU entity, you can often use reverse-charge mechanisms, but having a local presence simplifies tax compliance for large budgets.

items.title: Thuiswinkel Waarborg
items.text: The leading trust mark for e-commerce in the Netherlands. Displaying this badge can increase conversion rates by up to 15%.

items.title: Sustainability is Key
items.text: Dutch consumers are environmentally conscious. Highlighting sustainable shipping or packaging in marketing is highly effective.

items.title: Spam Laws (ACM)
items.text: The Netherlands has very strict opt-in laws. Cold emailing B2B leads without prior consent is heavily fined.
